quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The next rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane before starting to pass. All riders should follow this pattern until they have passed the vehicle.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. These signs show road rules that you must follow.

questions.question: When carrying a load in a sidecar, you should:

options.text: Secure the load so it does not shift.
Place the load loosely in the seat.
Secure the load at the front of the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the load so it does not shift.
questions.explanation: Secure loads in the sidecar so they do not move. Place the load toward the rear of the sidecar to prevent the nose from dipping during sharp left turns.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, your passenger should:

options.text: Sit on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Not sit on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit in the sidecar.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Which of the following should you NOT do to improve safety when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are near, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you. Their headlights can help light the road, and their taillights show if there are bumps ahead.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. Use your left foot to shift. Lift the lever to shift to a higher gear. Press the lever down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Both the front and rear brakes.
Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best way to stay close while keeping safe distance is to ride:
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while maintaining safe distance. Use a single-file line when riding around curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: What color are warning signs, and what color is the lettering?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A car is entering the highway from an entrance ramp on your right. The driver may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the left portion of your lane so they can share the lane, if necessary.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give plenty of room to vehicles entering the highway. Move to another lane if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to enter safely.

questions.question: What is true about the front brake on a motorcycle?

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should be used only under slippery conditions.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use, if used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use, if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes any time you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It is safe if you use it correctly.

questions.question: You cannot avoid an object or uneven surface on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Make sure the motorcycle is leaning to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat to allow your legs to absorb the shock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat to allow your legs to absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can. Keep the motorcycle straight up. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb the impact. Just before hitting the obstacle, roll on the throttle a little to lift the front wheel.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time the rider is slowing or stopping
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time the rider is slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you see when you adjust your mirrors correctly?

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. You may see a small part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: Your motorcycle starts to wobble. What should you do?

options.text: Keep riding, as the wobble will likely correct itself.
Close the throttle to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can and fix the problem causing the wobble.

questions.question: Where should you get the most information about your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. Read the manual before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on most motorcycles?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you start riding.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: Eliminates your ability to change direction.
Is only a concern if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Eliminates your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is very dangerous and can cause a crash and serious injury or death. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. Once locked, you cannot steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their motorcycle.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. The safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space around your motorcycle and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, a horn:

options.text: Usually cannot be heard by others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can quickly get someone's attention.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn. Other drivers may not hear it. Never rely only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: To lower the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you and understand what you plan to do. Signal clearly and position yourself well in your lane. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch for hazards ahead. Be ready to react quickly.

questions.question: If a rider in a group wants to ride faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a planned location later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Split up so each rider can go their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a planned location later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster than the group, let them ride ahead. The group should meet at a planned location later.

questions.question: To properly control a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so your arms hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the fuel tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the fuel tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can easily reach all controls. Keep your arms slightly bent and use them to steer, not to hold yourself up. Press your knees against the fuel tank to help you balance during turns.
